$comment: NON-NORMATIVE. This vocabulary is a conformance-suite diagnostic aid, not part of the CDX specification. The specification mandates DISPOSITIONS (State Machine section 5.4) and lineage OUTCOMES (Provenance and Lineage section 3.3) — never error identifiers. A conforming implementation is free to use its own internal errors and map them to these codes in its conformance adapter; it is never required to adopt this vocabulary. A code sharpens a failure report and is never by itself the pass criterion for a MUST — the normative assertion is the `disposition` each entry records.

compatibilityPolicy.summary: Codes are append-only and permanently stable once published.
rules: A code is NEVER re-pointed at a different defect. If the meaning must change, a new code is added and the old one is deprecated.
A deprecated code keeps its entry forever, gaining `deprecated: true` and, where applicable, `supersededBy`. Entries are never deleted.

`version` is the vocabulary's own semantic version and bumps on any addition, any deprecation, and any erratum-driven change to a published entry (a re-synced `clause`/`dispositionClause`, a null disposition made concrete, or a narrowed `summary`). Without the last clause a pure-erratum commit could turn a loadable document into a rejected one with `version` unchanged, which is exactly the silent change this policy exists to prevent.
`specVersion` is the CDX specification version the `clause` citations resolve against.

ERRATA. When a specification erratum amends a clause an entry cites, `clause` and `dispositionClause` are RE-SYNCED to the amended text and the change is recorded in CHANGELOG.md. A stale quotation is a false statement about the specification, and re-quoting changes no classification, so this is not a re-pointing. A `note` may likewise be rewritten at any time.

ERRATA. A `disposition` of null may become concrete when an erratum closes the gap that made it null — the specification now assigns a row where it previously assigned none. This is the gap closing, not a reclassification. The reverse is NOT permitted, and a concrete disposition is NEVER changed to a different concrete disposition; that is a re-pointing and requires a new code.

ERRATA. A `summary` may be NARROWED when an erratum moves one of its enumerated arms to a new code, provided BOTH entries record the move. Narrowing only: a summary is never widened to absorb a further defect class, and never re-pointed. The alternative — freezing a summary that now describes coverage the code no longer has — protects no consumer, because such a consumer would map the moved arm to this code and under-report its disposition.

A section 5.4.2 row is cited by QUOTING its text, never by row or line number. The table's numbering shifts whenever a row is inserted, so a numeric citation silently rots — as `CDX-E-ASSET-INDEX-UNUSABLE`'s did.

dispositionNote: `disposition` records the load-time disposition the SPECIFICATION assigns to this defect class (State Machine section 5.4), with `dispositionClause` naming the row relied on. It is the normative half of an entry. A null disposition means the specification assigns no document-level disposition to this defect — not that a consumer may ignore it. NOTE for STATE-VARYING rows: a few section 5.4.2 rows assign different dispositions by document state (e.g. a structurally malformed block/mark of a known type is WARNING in draft/review but INTEGRITY-ERROR in frozen/published). The scalar `disposition` records the state-invariant or draft/review disposition; any frozen/published escalation is described in `note` pending a state-aware model. This is a widening of an entry's stated disposition for higher-integrity states, not a re-pointing of the code to a different defect, so it is compatible with the append-only policy. NOTE for lineage entries: the lineage OUTCOME vocabulary (VERIFIED/INCOMPLETE/REJECTED, Provenance and Lineage section 3.3) is a different axis from the DISPOSITION vocabulary (IGNORE/WARNING/INTEGRITY-ERROR/REJECT). A lineage outcome of REJECTED does NOT mean the disposition REJECT: a proven-forged lineage is a WARNING, because the document's content identity is unaffected and it is not blocked on lineage grounds.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-ID-PENDING.summary: A manifest projection was requested for a document whose id is still `pending`.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-ID-PENDING.dispositionClause: Not a document defect: the manifest is well-formed and the projection is simply undefined until the document id is assigned. No load-time disposition applies.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-ID-PENDING.note: The projection is defined only once the document id is fixed.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-HASH-MALFORMED.summary: A declared content hash is absent, or is not a well-formed `algorithm:hexdigest`.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-HASH-MALFORMED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (manifest absent, unparseable, or missing or mistyping a required field)

CDX-E-MANIFEST-REFERENCE-MALFORMED.summary: A declared file reference is not a well-formed `{path, hash}` object (not an object, or a missing/non-string path).
CDX-E-MANIFEST-REFERENCE-MALFORMED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (manifest absent, unparseable, or missing or mistyping a required field)
CDX-E-MANIFEST-REFERENCE-MALFORMED.note: Distinct from CDX-E-MANIFEST-HASH-MALFORMED: the defect is the shape of the reference, not the hash value. ALSO emitted for a MISTYPED `metadata` object or `metadata.dublinCore` path: both are required manifest fields (Manifest section 4.11), so a present-but-wrong-typed one is State Machine section 5.4.2's "manifest ... missing or mistyping a required field" REJECT. That reference is a bare relative-path string rather than a `{path, hash}` object, so the summary's shape does not describe it; the defect CLASS is the same — a manifest reference that cannot be interpreted — which is why this code is reused rather than a new one minted, the append-only policy forbidding a code from being re-pointed but not from covering a further instance of its own class.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-PATH-TRAVERSAL.summary: A declared path is not a safe archive-relative path (escapes the archive root).
CDX-E-MANIFEST-PATH-TRAVERSAL.clause: Security Extension section 9.7; Container Format section 9.1
CDX-E-MANIFEST-PATH-TRAVERSAL.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (an unsafe archive path or symlink always REJECTs, in every state)

CDX-E-MANIFEST-VERSION-MALFORMED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (manifest absent, unparseable, or missing or mistyping a required field)

CDX-E-MANIFEST-STATE-UNKNOWN.clause: State Machine section 3.1; Security Extension section 9.7
CDX-E-MANIFEST-STATE-UNKNOWN.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (a `state` value outside the defined lifecycle enum, so the mutability-and-signature contract cannot be established)

CDX-E-MANIFEST-EXTENSION-DUPLICATE.summary: Two `manifest.extensions[]` entries share an id, making the projection ambiguous.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-EXTENSION-DUPLICATE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 assigns NO row to this defect class. The projection fails closed on it (the projected bytes would otherwise be ambiguous), but the specification does not state a load-time disposition and none is inferred here — notably the generic "missing or mistyping a required field" row does not reach it, since section 5.4.2 gives the `state` enum its own dedicated row rather than relying on that one. Tracked as a specification gap.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-REFERENCE-HASH-CONFLICT.note: Emitted for the config-file references and the asset-index references.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-ABSENT.summary: The archive contains no `manifest.json` entry, so the document has no manifest to load.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-ABSENT.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (manifest absent, unparseable, or missing or mistyping a required field)

CDX-E-MANIFEST-UNPARSEABLE.summary: `manifest.json` is present but is not well-formed JSON (a bare syntax error), or is valid JSON that is not an object, so it cannot be parsed as a manifest.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-UNPARSEABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (manifest absent, unparseable, or missing or mistyping a required field)
CDX-E-MANIFEST-UNPARSEABLE.note: Distinct from CDX-E-PART-DUPLICATE-KEYS, which is a canonical-JSON violation detected structurally rather than a JSON syntax error, and from CDX-E-MANIFEST-*-MALFORMED, which fire on a parseable manifest OBJECT with a bad field.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-FIELD-MISSING.summary: A required manifest field is absent: the `metadata` object, or `metadata.dublinCore` within it.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-FIELD-MISSING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (manifest absent, unparseable, or missing or mistyping a required field).
CDX-E-MANIFEST-FIELD-MISSING.note: SCOPE MOVE RECORDED (the append-only errata rule requires both entries to record it): the no-reference-at-all arm was previously carried by CDX-E-METADATA-PART-MISSING at WARNING, whose summary has been narrowed to the referenced-but-absent arm it keeps. MISSING is this code; MISTYPED is CDX-E-MANIFEST-REFERENCE-MALFORMED, whose published summary describes a DECLARED reference that is malformed and so does not describe an absent field. Both are the same REJECT row. This split settles an ambiguity the vocabulary previously recorded rather than resolved: `metadata` is required by the manifest schema and `dublinCore` is required within it, so an absent one is a malformed manifest, exactly as an absent `content` is. The section 5.4.2 metadata row is now explicitly PART-level — a referenced-but-absent or unparseable Dublin Core part, or a missing required term — and keeps its narrower WARNING under CDX-E-METADATA-PART-MISSING. This code is also the right home for any future absent-required-field arm.

CDX-E-PART-DUPLICATE-KEYS.summary: A JSON part contains an object with duplicate keys, which the canonical-JSON rules forbid before any hashing or verification.
CDX-E-PART-DUPLICATE-KEYS.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (duplicate JSON keys in any part always REJECT, in every state)
CDX-E-PART-DUPLICATE-KEYS.note: An unrejected duplicate key permits a split-view substitution — one key-value pair is hashed while a colliding one is materialized — so the rejection is state-invariant, exactly like a duplicate archive entry.

CDX-E-PART-NUMBER-NON-REPRESENTABLE.summary: A hashed JSON number is non-finite, or an integer whose magnitude exceeds 2^53 - 1, so the IEEE-754 double the canonicalizer hashes would differ from the value the author wrote.
CDX-E-PART-NUMBER-NON-REPRESENTABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (a non-representable hashed number always REJECTs, in every state)

CDX-E-PART-STRING-ILL-FORMED.summary: A hashed object key or string value is not well-formed Unicode — it carries an unpaired surrogate code point, so it has no UTF-8 encoding at all.
CDX-E-PART-STRING-ILL-FORMED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (a stored-byte Unicode violation always REJECTs, in every state)
CDX-E-PART-STRING-ILL-FORMED.note: STATE-INVARIANT, and a split-view substitution rather than a producer slip: RFC 8259 parsers disagree on such an escape exactly as they disagree on a duplicate key — one preserves the lone surrogate, another substitutes U+FFFD, a third refuses the input — so two conformant readers derive different canonical bytes, and therefore different document IDs, from one archive. SCOPE IS THE HASHED MATERIAL of a part, which is the stored bytes MINUS the fields canonicalization deletes. Section 4.3.2 states NFC and well-formedness as properties of the stored bytes, and both summaries above bind a HASHED key or value: a field the canonical transform DELETES — a `crdt` value, a `measurement` `display`, a `codeBlock` `tokens` — is not hashed, and no violation in one is reported. The split-view harm cannot reach such a field either, since two readers cannot derive different canonical bytes from a field both delete; the conformance fixture `positive-content-derived-field-non-nfc` is the published control for exactly this boundary, and a reader scanning the whole stored part rejects that conformant document in every state. A field the transform REWRITES rather than deletes is different and IS reported: an asset path resolved to a content hash (section 4.3.1 item 2) is replaced before validation runs, so the canonicalizer never sees the stored path while section 4.3.2 still binds it. THE THIRD ARM OF THE SAME CLAUSE DIFFERS, deliberately: CDX-E-PART-NUMBER-NON-REPRESENTABLE is scanned over the whole raw stored part, deleted fields included. It was published that way and narrowing it would flip an expectation an implementation may already meet, so the two arms are out of step by decision rather than oversight.

CDX-E-PART-STRING-NOT-NFC.summary: A hashed object key or string value is not in Normalization Form C — either individually, or in the concatenated text content of a block, where a combining sequence split across a text-node boundary leaves each node's own value NFC while their concatenation is not.
CDX-E-PART-STRING-NOT-NFC.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (a stored-byte Unicode violation always REJECTs, in every state)
CDX-E-PART-STRING-NOT-NFC.note: STATE-INVARIANT. Section 4.3.2 makes NFC a property of the stored bytes and forbids normalizing at hash time, so a reader has no repair available — normalizing would change the very bytes the document is identified by, which is why this is not a warning. Character offsets are defined over NFC text (Anchors and References section 3), so a non-NFC block also leaves every anchor, range, and annotation addressing it pointing into text the document does not contain. Scope is the HASHED material, exactly as for CDX-E-PART-STRING-ILL-FORMED: a violation in a field the canonical transform DELETES is not reported, one in a field it REWRITES is. See that entry for the boundary and for why the number arm of the same clause does not match it. This arm additionally checks the CONCATENATED text of a run of adjacent text nodes, since section 4.3.2 applies NFC to a block's whole text content — a combining sequence split across a text-node boundary leaves every individual string in NFC while their concatenation is not. The run arm carries a THIRD condition the per-string arm does not: POSITION. It applies only where the schemas declare block content (a block's `children`, the root `blocks`, a figure's rich `caption`, an exercise's `hints`, an exercise set's `preamble`, a footnote mark's `content`), because a run of text nodes only means a block's text content there. Objects that merely RESEMBLE text nodes elsewhere — most reachably inside `attributes.semantic`, a JSON-LD annotation open to any member name — are data, and a reader that concatenates them rejects conformant documents. The per-string checks still apply to every hashed string at any position, including those; only the run is withheld.

CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-MISSING.summary: The required content part is absent: `manifest.content.path` is a valid archive-relative path but names no existing archive entry.
CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-MISSING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (missing the required content part)
CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-MISSING.note: A missing or non-string content reference is caught earlier as CDX-E-MANIFEST-REFERENCE-MALFORMED; this code fires only when the reference is well-formed but no entry backs the path. An encrypted content part mapped to a stored `.enc` entry by the security extension satisfies the presence requirement (State Machine section 5.4.2 note 5).

CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-UNPARSEABLE.summary: The content part is present but cannot be parsed as JSON — a bare syntax error, or a decompression / parser-resource-limit failure — so the content and the document's identity cannot be established.
CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-UNPARSEABLE.clause: Document Hashing section 4.3.2; State Machine section 5.4.1
CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-UNPARSEABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.1 (a document that cannot be parsed, or whose identity cannot be established, is a REJECT): the content part is required canonical JSON (Document Hashing section 4.3.2), so a content part that cannot be parsed yields no canonical content in any state — and, once an id is assigned, makes its recomputation impossible.
CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-UNPARSEABLE.note: Distinct from CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-MISSING (no entry backs the path), CDX-E-PART-DUPLICATE-KEYS (a canonical-JSON structural violation with its own code), and CDX-E-CONTENT-ROOT-MALFORMED (the part PARSES but violates its root envelope). That last boundary is the one an adapter is most likely to get wrong: this code is for bytes that do not yield a JSON value at all, never for a JSON value of the wrong shape. Scoped to the required content part; a missing or unparseable NON-content part (Dublin Core, presentation) is a separate later-phase disposition.

CDX-E-CONTENT-ROOT-MALFORMED.summary: The content part parses as JSON but violates the content root envelope: the parsed value is not an object, or `version` or `blocks` is absent or of the wrong JSON type.
CDX-E-CONTENT-ROOT-MALFORMED.clause: Content Blocks sections 2.2, 7.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-CONTENT-ROOT-MALFORMED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (the `content` part is present and parses, but violates the content root envelope — the parsed value is not a JSON object, or `version` or `blocks` is absent or of the wrong JSON type — REJECT). State-invariant.
CDX-E-CONTENT-ROOT-MALFORMED.note: The root is OPEN: Content Blocks section 2.2 requires `version` and `blocks` but content.schema.json declares no root `additionalProperties: false`, so an unrecognized root member is NOT this defect. The `version` VALUE is likewise not covered — only its type. A well-formed `version` carrying a bad value ("0.1.0", "9.9") is a different defect class that State Machine section 5.4.2 assigns no row: its version rows govern the manifest `cdx` field, not the content model version, so reporting it would mean choosing a disposition the specification does not state. A mistyped `blocks` is the arm that matters most: every content-level row in the section 5.4.2 table is reached by walking `blocks`, so a non-array withdraws all of them at once while the document id stays computable and a signature over it still verifies.

CDX-E-VERSION-MAJOR-UNSUPPORTED.summary: The manifest `cdx` field declares a major format version this reader does not implement, so the document cannot be safely interpreted.

CDX-E-VERSION-MINOR-UNSUPPORTED.summary: The manifest `cdx` field declares a minor format version newer than this reader implements; known fields are processed and unknown additions ignored.
CDX-E-VERSION-MINOR-UNSUPPORTED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (unsupported minor version — process known fields, IGNORE unknown additions)

CDX-E-EXTENSION-REQUIRED-UNSUPPORTED.summary: A manifest extension marked `required: true` names a namespace this reader does not support, so the document cannot be fully interpreted.
CDX-E-EXTENSION-REQUIRED-UNSUPPORTED.note: An encrypted document declares cdx.security as required:true, so a reader without security-extension support rejects it through this row rather than misreading the archive (State Machine section 5.4.2 note 5).

CDX-E-EXTENSION-OPTIONAL-UNSUPPORTED.summary: A manifest extension marked `required: false` names a namespace this reader does not support; its data is skipped and the document degrades gracefully.
CDX-E-EXTENSION-OPTIONAL-UNSUPPORTED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (unsupported optional extension — degrade; SHOULD surface)

CDX-E-LINEAGE-CYCLE.summary: The lineage walk revisited a document already on the current path.
CDX-E-LINEAGE-CYCLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (REJECTED lineage — WARNING in every state)
CDX-E-LINEAGE-CYCLE.note: The lineage MUST be treated as forged — a verifier MUST NOT present any claimed ancestry as authenticated, and MUST surface the proven inconsistency as distinct from a merely unverifiable chain. The document's content identity is unaffected, so it is NOT blocked on lineage grounds: the outcome REJECTED is not the disposition REJECT.

CDX-E-LINEAGE-ANCESTORS-CONTRADICT.summary: A declared `ancestors` entry contradicts the resolved parent chain (forged tail).
CDX-E-LINEAGE-ANCESTORS-CONTRADICT.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (REJECTED lineage — WARNING in every state)
CDX-E-LINEAGE-ANCESTORS-CONTRADICT.note: Forged lineage: claimed ancestry MUST NOT be presented as authenticated, but the document is not blocked on lineage grounds. The outcome REJECTED is not the disposition REJECT.

CDX-E-LINEAGE-ROOT-WITH-ANCESTORS.summary: A document declaring no parent also declares a non-empty ancestors chain.
CDX-E-LINEAGE-ROOT-WITH-ANCESTORS.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (REJECTED lineage — WARNING in every state)
CDX-E-LINEAGE-ROOT-WITH-ANCESTORS.note: Forged lineage: claimed ancestry MUST NOT be presented as authenticated, but the document is not blocked on lineage grounds. The outcome REJECTED is not the disposition REJECT.

CDX-E-LINEAGE-UNRESOLVABLE.summary: A link in the chain could not be resolved, so the chain cannot be fully walked.
CDX-E-LINEAGE-UNRESOLVABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (INCOMPLETE lineage — WARNING in every state)
CDX-E-LINEAGE-UNRESOLVABLE.note: Unverified, never endorsed: no ancestor beyond the break is presented as verified. An unverifiable proof never rejects the document (section 5.4.3).

CDX-E-LINEAGE-BOUND-REACHED.summary: The traversal depth or breadth bound was reached before the walk completed.
CDX-E-LINEAGE-BOUND-REACHED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (INCOMPLETE lineage — WARNING in every state)
CDX-E-LINEAGE-BOUND-REACHED.note: A legitimately deep or wide history is not an inconsistency.

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-UNREADABLE.summary: The archive cannot be parsed as a ZIP: no End Of Central Directory record, or a truncated or malformed central directory.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-UNREADABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Archive unreadable ... REJECT in every state)

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DUPLICATE-ENTRY.summary: Two central-directory entries resolve to the same path after the section 3.4 normalization.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DUPLICATE-ENTRY.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (Duplicate archive entries always REJECT, in every state)
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DUPLICATE-ENTRY.note: Closes a split-view substitution: a signer's tooling hashes one entry into the document id while a victim's reader materializes a different entry of the same name under one still-valid signature.

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-CASE-COLLISION.summary: Two central-directory entries differ only in case, colliding when extracted onto a case-insensitive filesystem.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-CASE-COLLISION.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (Duplicate archive entries, including a case-only collision, always REJECT, in every state)

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-LFH-CD-DISAGREEMENT.summary: The local-file-header view and the central-directory view disagree on the entry set: a central entry with no matching local header, or a local name that differs from its central name.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-LFH-CD-DISAGREEMENT.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (local-file-header/central-directory entry-set disagreement always REJECTs, in every state)

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DATA-OUTSIDE-CD.summary: A local file header exists that the central directory does not enumerate (file data outside the authoritative index).
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DATA-OUTSIDE-CD.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (local-file-header/central-directory entry-set disagreement always REJECTs, in every state)
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DATA-OUTSIDE-CD.note: The central directory is the authoritative index; a stray local entry is a split-view substitution vector.

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-UNSAFE-NAME.summary: An archive entry name fails the section 9.1 safety checks: a `..` segment, an absolute or drive/UNC/colon-bearing name, a backslash, a reserved Windows device name, a trailing dot/space segment, or an overlong or ill-formed UTF-8 encoding.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-UNSAFE-NAME.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (an unsafe archive path or symlink always REJECTs, in every state)

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-SYMLINK-ENTRY.summary: An archive entry encodes a symbolic link (a Unix mode with the symlink bit set).
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-SYMLINK-ENTRY.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (an unsafe archive path or symlink always REJECTs, in every state)
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-SYMLINK-ENTRY.note: CDX defines no legitimate use for a symlink entry; it is a second path-traversal vector.

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DECOMPRESSION-BOMB.summary: A declared entry size, decompression ratio, or archive total exceeds the reader's finite bound.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DECOMPRESSION-BOMB.dispositionClause: Container Format sections 5.3 and 9.2 (a conforming reader MUST enforce a finite bound on every attacker-controlled dimension and MUST fail closed -- reject the archive -- when one is exceeded). Section 5.4.2 does not itself enumerate this class; the disposition is stated in the mechanism sections.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DECOMPRESSION-BOMB.note: The specific thresholds are implementation-defined (section 5.1 gives reasonable defaults); the existence and enforcement of a bound is the requirement. A fixture bomb must exceed any plausible conformant bound, not one specific threshold.

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-CRC-MISMATCH.summary: A stored ZIP CRC-32 does not match the CRC recomputed over the entry's actual bytes (a corrupt entry).
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-CRC-MISMATCH.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (ZIP CRC-32 mismatch for an archive entry). The stored bytes cannot be trusted to decompress to the content they claim, independently of the semantic document hash (section 6.2).

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-FIRST-FILE-NOT-MANIFEST.summary: The first archive entry is not `manifest.json`.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-FIRST-FILE-NOT-MANIFEST.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (the first archive entry is not manifest.json). The archive is fully readable and the manifest resolvable by name, so only the streaming/quick-validation optimization is lost.

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-ENCRYPTION-USED.summary: An entry uses ZIP-level encryption (general-purpose bit 0 set); CDX uses the security extension for encryption, never the container.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-ENCRYPTION-USED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (ZIP-level encryption present, or a multi-volume archive, both forbidden by Container Format section 3.1 and neither coherently loadable)

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-MULTI-VOLUME.summary: The archive is a multi-volume (split) ZIP: an End Of Central Directory disk field is non-zero.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-MULTI-VOLUME.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (ZIP-level encryption present, or a multi-volume archive, both forbidden by Container Format section 3.1 and neither coherently loadable)

CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.summary: A content block has an unrecognized but well-formed namespaced type (`ns:name`, e.g. `myorg:widget`) — an extension block type this reader does not implement.
CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.clause: Content Blocks section 5; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (unknown namespaced block or mark type — IGNORE, render a fallback). State-invariant.
CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.note: "Namespaced" is the schema's extension-type form (a non-empty prefix, a colon, a non-empty suffix); a registered namespaced type such as academic:theorem is in the known set and is NOT reported here (Content Blocks section 5.1 line 1019).

CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.summary: A content block has an unrecognized type that is not a well-formed namespaced identifier: a bare or misspelled type (e.g. `paragrph`), a colon-malformed type (`:x`, `x:`), a missing or non-string `type`, or a non-object in a block position — none of which can be deferred to an extension fallback.
CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.clause: Content Blocks section 5; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (unknown bare, non-namespaced block or mark type — REJECT). State-invariant; Content Blocks section 5.1 line 1017 frames the bare-vs-namespaced split so a misspelled core type is caught rather than silently accepted.
CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.note: Fail-closed: only a well-formed namespaced identifier earns the lenient IGNORE of CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED; every other unrecognized block type is bare and REJECTs.

CDX-E-BLOCK-MALFORMED.summary: A block of a KNOWN CORE type violates a structural constraint JSON Schema cannot express: upward containment (e.g. a `tableCell`, `tableRow`, or `figcaption` outside its required parent), figure / definitionItem cardinality, or a node-bearing field of the wrong shape — on the block or on one of its subfigures — (`children`/`subfigures`/`marks` present but not an array, `caption` present but neither array nor string, or a `subfigures` element that is not an object).
CDX-E-BLOCK-MALFORMED.clause: Content Blocks section 7.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-BLOCK-MALFORMED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (structurally malformed block or mark of a known type — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-BLOCK-MALFORMED.note: This code carries the DRAFT/REVIEW disposition only. The FROZEN/PUBLISHED escalation to INTEGRITY-ERROR is gated on a valid signature (State Machine section 5.3) and is deferred to B3; every B1b-2 fixture is a draft.

CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.summary: A text-node mark has an unrecognized but well-formed namespaced type (`ns:name`, e.g. `myorg:flag`), in either bare-string or typed-object form — an extension mark this reader does not implement.
CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.clause: Content Blocks section 5.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (unknown namespaced block or mark type — IGNORE, render the unmarked text). State-invariant.
CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.note: A registered namespaced mark such as legal:cite is in the known set and is NOT reported here (Content Blocks section 5.1 line 1019).

CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.summary: A text-node mark has an unrecognized type that is not a well-formed namespaced identifier: a bare or misspelled mark string (e.g. `itlaic`), a colon-malformed mark, a mark object with a missing or non-string `type`, or a mark that is neither a string nor an object.
CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.clause: Content Blocks section 5.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (unknown bare, non-namespaced block or mark type — REJECT). State-invariant; Content Blocks section 5.1 line 1017: an unrecognized bare mark is rejected as malformed, so a misspelled core mark is not silently accepted as an unknown mark.
CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.note: Fail-closed: only a well-formed namespaced identifier earns the lenient IGNORE of CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED; every other unrecognized mark type is bare and REJECTs.

CDX-E-MARK-MALFORMED.summary: A mark of a KNOWN type is structurally malformed for that type: a core structured mark missing a required field (`link` without `href`, `anchor` without `id`, `math` without `format`/`source`), a core string mark (bold, italic, …) carried as an object, or a structured mark used as a bare string.
CDX-E-MARK-MALFORMED.clause: Content Blocks section 5.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-MARK-MALFORMED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (structurally malformed block or mark of a known type — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-MARK-MALFORMED.note: This code carries the DRAFT/REVIEW disposition only; the FROZEN/PUBLISHED INTEGRITY-ERROR escalation is deferred to B3 (State Machine section 5.3). The internal field validation of the registered EXTENSION structured marks (citation, footnote, entity, glossary, academic:*-ref, presentation:*, legal:cite) is deferred; those types are in the known set, so they are neither rejected nor ignored.

CDX-E-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH.summary: A declared file-level hash does not match the exact stored bytes it pins: the digest of the content part's raw decompressed bytes, under the algorithm named by the hash's own prefix (Document Hashing section 3.3), differs from `manifest.content.hash`.
CDX-E-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH.clause: Document Hashing sections 5.1, 6.3; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (File `hash` or document-ID mismatch — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH.note: STATE-VARYING: the DRAFT/REVIEW disposition is WARNING; on a FROZEN/PUBLISHED document it escalates to INTEGRITY-ERROR (state-keyed per Document Hashing section 6.3 — the document asserts fixed, integrity-checked bytes). The escalation is deferred to B3: soundly trusting `state = frozen`/`published` requires a projection-covering signature (State Machine section 5.4.2 note 3, lifecycle-downgrade), which needs B2 trust material. B1b-3a verifies the file-level `content.hash`, which is what this code's summary is scoped to; the asset-index, asset, presentation-file and config-side-file hashes are verified under their own codes (CDX-E-ASSET-INDEX-HASH-MISMATCH, CDX-E-ASSET-HASH-MISMATCH, CDX-E-PRESENTATION-HASH-MISMATCH, CDX-E-CONFIG-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH), added in B1b-3b-2 rather than folded in here — widening a published summary is the kind of re-pointing the append-only policy forbids.

CDX-E-DOCUMENT-ID-MISMATCH.summary: The document ID recomputed from the canonical content (Document Hashing section 4) does not equal the declared `manifest.id`.
CDX-E-DOCUMENT-ID-MISMATCH.clause: Document Hashing sections 4.4, 6.3, 7.2; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-DOCUMENT-ID-MISMATCH.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (File `hash` or document-ID mismatch — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-DOCUMENT-ID-MISMATCH.note: STATE-VARYING: WARNING in DRAFT/REVIEW, escalating to INTEGRITY-ERROR on FROZEN/PUBLISHED (state-keyed per Document Hashing section 6.3; deferred to B3 via State Machine section 5.4.2 note 3, as for CDX-E-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH). Recomputed only for a document carrying a real id — a draft's id is `pending` (Document Hashing section 7.1) and has nothing to recompute. A *stale* id (one computed over earlier content or metadata) is exactly what this row detects; a review/frozen/published document carrying a `pending` id is instead a section 7.2 violation this row does not catch, since a pending id is skipped rather than recomputed.

CDX-E-METADATA-PART-MISSING.summary: The Dublin Core metadata part is referenced by `metadata.dublinCore` but the path it declares names no archive entry.
CDX-E-METADATA-PART-MISSING.clause: Metadata sections 3.3.1, 3.3.2; Container Format section 3.3.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-METADATA-PART-MISSING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Missing required metadata at the PART level — the Dublin Core part is referenced but absent or unparseable, or a required term is missing — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-METADATA-PART-MISSING.note: STATE-VARYING: WARNING in DRAFT/REVIEW, escalating to INTEGRITY-ERROR on FROZEN/PUBLISHED, where the projected Dublin Core terms enter the document ID and the document asserts them fixed. The escalation is deferred to B3 via State Machine section 5.4.2 note 3, which requires a projection-covering signature before `state` can be trusted. AMBIGUITY SETTLED: this code previously also covered the no-reference-at-all case, recording that `metadata.dublinCore` is a REQUIRED manifest field and so also read as the section 5.4.2 'Manifest ... missing ... a required field' REJECT. The erratum took that reading: an absent `metadata` or `metadata.dublinCore` field is now CDX-E-MANIFEST-FIELD-MISSING at REJECT, and the metadata row is explicitly PART-level. This code keeps its own defect and its WARNING — a Dublin Core part that is REFERENCED but names no archive entry. Per State Machine section 5.4.2 note 5, an encrypted part mapped to a stored `.enc` entry satisfies presence and MUST NOT fire this code; that mapping arrives with the security extension's part handling.

CDX-E-METADATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.summary: The Dublin Core metadata part cannot be used as Dublin Core: a syntax error, a resource-limit failure, a valid JSON value that is not an object, or an object the metadata projection REJECTS — a non-object `terms`, a wrong-typed `title`/`description`, or a `creator`/`subject`/`language` that is neither a string nor an array of strings.
CDX-E-METADATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.clause: Metadata section 3; Document Hashing section 4.3.2; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-METADATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Missing required metadata at the PART level — the Dublin Core part is referenced but absent or unparseable, or a required term is missing — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-METADATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.note: STATE-VARYING exactly as CDX-E-METADATA-PART-MISSING: WARNING in DRAFT/REVIEW, INTEGRITY-ERROR on FROZEN/PUBLISHED, deferred to B3. An unreadable part is treated as unavailable rather than as empty metadata: the document ID projects the real terms, so recomputing over an empty projection would compare a different document's basis and manufacture a spurious CDX-E-DOCUMENT-ID-MISMATCH. The id is therefore reported as indeterminate, not mismatched. A DUPLICATE KEY in the part is not this code — it is the state-invariant REJECT CDX-E-PART-DUPLICATE-KEYS (State Machine section 5.4.3). The unprojectable-term arm is reported here rather than as a missing term because the projection THROWS on it: the metadata cannot enter the document ID at all, so the id is indeterminate. Left unreported it would silently disable the document-ID check from inside the recompute's error handling, which one malformed ADVISORY term would then be enough to switch off.

CDX-E-METADATA-TERM-MISSING.summary: The Dublin Core part loads but omits a term the specification requires: `title` (a non-empty string) or `creator` (at least one value, in either the scalar or the array form).
CDX-E-METADATA-TERM-MISSING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Missing required metadata at the PART level — the Dublin Core part is referenced but absent or unparseable, or a required term is missing — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-METADATA-TERM-MISSING.note: STATE-VARYING as for the other two metadata codes: WARNING in DRAFT/REVIEW, INTEGRITY-ERROR on FROZEN/PUBLISHED, deferred to B3. The part still parses, so the document ID remains computable and is verified normally — a missing term lowers metadata quality without making the identity indeterminate. Only `title` and `creator` are required; every other Dublin Core term is optional (Metadata section 3.3).

CDX-E-PART-MISSING-UNBOUND.summary: A manifest reference that carries a path but NO hash names an archive entry that does not exist — the provenance record, a `metadata.jsonld` side file, a collaboration comments or changes file, or the phantom clusters file.
CDX-E-PART-MISSING-UNBOUND.clause: Security Extension section 9.8; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-PART-MISSING-UNBOUND.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Missing a referenced part outside the document hash and manifest projection — WARNING in every state).
CDX-E-PART-MISSING-UNBOUND.note: STATE-INVARIANT: WARNING in draft, review, frozen and published alike. A path-only reference binds nothing — the target is in neither the document hash nor the manifest projection (extensions overview, Integrity Status of Extension Data) — so its absence degrades a layer and cannot signal tampering. This is deliberately NOT the hash-BOUND missing-part row (a declared presentation layer, an asset index), which escalates to INTEGRITY-ERROR when frozen and is verified in B1b-3b-2. A part that is present but unparseable is CDX-E-EXTENSION-DATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE, not this code. `security.signatures` and `security.encryption` are path-only too but are verified with B2's trust material. Per State Machine section 5.4.2 note 5, an encrypted part mapped to a stored `.enc` entry satisfies presence and MUST NOT fire this code.

CDX-E-EXTENSION-DATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.summary: An out-of-hash extension data part — a collaboration comments or changes file, a phantom clusters file, form data, or the core annotations file — is present but is not well-formed JSON.
CDX-E-EXTENSION-DATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.clause: Extensions overview (Integrity Status of Extension Data, Out-of-hash version skew); State Machine sections 5.4.2, 5.4.3
CDX-E-EXTENSION-DATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Missing or unparseable out-of-hash extension data part — WARNING in every state).
CDX-E-EXTENSION-DATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.note: STATE-INVARIANT: these bytes sit in no signature scope and in no hash, so a defect in them can never signal tampering — the extensions overview states directly that a missing or unparseable out-of-hash data part is a WARNING in all states and MUST NOT be reported as an INTEGRITY-ERROR. Scoped to the conventional out-of-hash locations (`collaboration/`, `phantoms/`, `forms/`, `security/annotations.json`) plus any path the manifest declares for them; an unrecognized file elsewhere in the archive is IGNORE (State Machine section 5.4.2), never this code. A DUPLICATE KEY in such a part remains the state-invariant REJECT CDX-E-PART-DUPLICATE-KEYS (State Machine section 5.4.3): an unrejected duplicate permits a split-view substitution regardless of which layer carries it.

CDX-E-ANCHOR-DANGLING.summary: A core anchor reference in hashed content resolves to no block or anchor id in the document: a `link` mark whose `href` begins `#` and names an identifier the content does not define.
CDX-E-ANCHOR-DANGLING.clause: Anchors and References sections 7.2, 2.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-ANCHOR-DANGLING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling core anchor reference in hashed content — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-ANCHOR-DANGLING.note: STATE-VARYING: WARNING in DRAFT/REVIEW, escalating to INTEGRITY-ERROR on FROZEN/PUBLISHED (Anchors and References section 7.2 states this directly — content is fluid below frozen, so a target may not exist yet; above it, a broken anchor indicates corruption). The escalation is deferred to B3 via State Machine section 5.4.2 note 3. A core anchor is part of the document's addressing layer, so a dangling one is an internal-consistency failure of signed content — unlike an extension cross-reference (CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-DANGLING), which only degrades rendering. A reference that does not begin `#` addresses nothing in this document and is not a defect. Offset and range validity within a resolved target (Anchors and References section 7.3) is a SEPARATE check with its own codes: CDX-E-ANCHOR-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE for a position past the target's text, CDX-E-ANCHOR-POSITION-INVALID for a structurally invalid one. Those fire independently of this code — a reference can be both dangling and malformed, and reporting only the dangle would conceal the second defect. The out-of-range code is scoped to this row's fields exactly as this one is, the other two rows having their own (CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE, CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE): a position defect is disposed of by the row of the FIELD carrying it, not by a row of its own.

CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-DANGLING.summary: A Content Anchor URI carried in an extension BLOCK field resolves to no block or anchor id: `academic:proof` `of`, an `academic:theorem` `uses[]` element, or a `semantic:ref` or `presentation:reference` `target`.
CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-DANGLING.clause: Anchors and References sections 7.2, 11; Academic Extension section 9; Document Hashing section 4.3.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-DANGLING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling core anchor reference in hashed content — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-DANGLING.note: STATE-VARYING as CDX-E-ANCHOR-DANGLING, and deferred to B3 on the same grounds. CLASSIFICATION RECORDED AS CONTESTED, which is why these fields carry their own code rather than sharing CDX-E-ANCHOR-DANGLING. They are treated here as core anchors: Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 5 rewrites them into the same relabelled identifier namespace as a `link` mark, and State Machine section 5.4.2's extension-cross-reference carve-out names only MARKS. Against that reading, Anchors and References section 11 groups `semantic:ref` and `presentation:reference` with the cross-reference mechanisms rather than with the core `link` mark, and section 5.4.2's preamble defines a core anchor as a `link` href, an `anchor` mark, or a STRUCTURED Content Anchor (the object form). Draft and review are WARNING under either reading, so the two differ only in the frozen column. THE FROZEN COLUMN IS SETTLED FOR TWO OF THE FOUR FIELDS, by a clause this entry formerly did not cite: Academic Extension section 9 states that a dangling `academic:proof` `of` or `academic:theorem` `uses` target is "a rendering-degradation WARNING in all states, not the FROZEN/PUBLISHED Error that Anchors and References section 7.2 assigns a dangling core anchor" — the disposition stated outright and section 7.2 rejected by name. Only `semantic:ref` `target` and `presentation:reference` `target` remain contested, which is also the pair section 11 names. A RISK IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN ACTED ON: that leaves ONE code spanning four fields whose frozen columns may diverge, since if B3 takes the core-anchor reading for those two they escalate while section 9 holds the other two at WARNING, and a single scalar disposition cannot carry both. Separating them is the remedy this entry's own reasoning prescribes, but unlike the position arm this code was PUBLISHED at v0.13, so the split is no longer free — closing it needs a successor code and a deprecation (compatibility policy rules 1 and 2), not a separation. An out-of-range POSITION in these same fields carries CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE; section 9 does NOT carry over to it, because both of section 9's sentences are scoped to a DANGLING target, so that entry's contest is WIDER than this one's rather than narrower.

CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-DANGLING.summary: An extension cross-reference mark resolved at render time points at nothing: an `academic:theorem-ref`, `academic:equation-ref`, or `academic:algorithm-ref` whose `target` Content Anchor URI names no defined identifier.
CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-DANGLING.clause: Anchors and References section 11; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-DANGLING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling extension cross-reference resolved at render time — WARNING in every state).
CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-DANGLING.note: STATE-INVARIANT: WARNING in every state, and State Machine section 5.4.2's preamble gives the reason — such a mark is resolved at render time to inject a label, number, or definition, so a dangling one degrades rendering only; the signed bytes remain intact and hash-verified. This is the disposition that distinguishes these marks from the core anchors of CDX-E-ANCHOR-DANGLING, which escalate — and it is what forces an out-of-range POSITION on one of these marks to carry its own code, CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE, rather than the core-anchor row's: sharing one would hold a stale offset to a harsher frozen-state disposition than a missing target, and that entry records the conflict Anchors and References section 7.2 raises against this row. COVERAGE IS NOW FOUR ARMS OF FIVE, and this code is scoped to the three `academic:*-ref` marks its summary enumerates. STILL UNCOVERED: the row also names a LEGAL cross-reference mark, and Legal Extension section 5 states the disposition for one — "a `legal:cite` whose `category` matches no Table of Authorities category" is among the relationships that "are rendering-degradation WARNINGs in all states, never integrity failures (State Machine section 5.4)". No code covers it and no resolver arm collects it. It is a different shape from the four that are covered: those resolve a reference against a namespace of ids or markers gathered from content or a side file, whereas this matches a `category` against a Table of Authorities CONFIGURATION, which raises its own question about whether an absent or unloadable configuration makes the namespace indeterminate. The other marks the same row names each have their own code, because their targets do not live in the content part and their namespaces are independent: a `citation` mark's `refs` address bibliography entry ids (CDX-E-CITATION-REFERENCE-DANGLING), a `glossary` mark's `ref` addresses the authoritative glossary source (CDX-E-GLOSSARY-REFERENCE-DANGLING) — both resolved in B1b-3b-2 — and a `footnote` mark resolves to a `semantic:footnote` block by id or marker (CDX-E-FOOTNOTE-REFERENCE-DANGLING, with CDX-E-FOOTNOTE-REFERENCE-AMBIGUOUS for a marker matching more than one). An earlier reading of this note called the footnote namespace an unspecified specification question; that was wrong — Semantic Extension section 4.5.2 had already settled it, and what was missing was only the resolver arm, now implemented.

CDX-E-ANCHOR-POSITION-INVALID.summary: An anchor in hashed content carries a structurally invalid position: a range whose start is not less than its end, a URI suffix that is neither an offset nor a range, a position on a target that names an `anchor` mark (which already denotes a position), or a position on a target that is not a text-bearing block.
CDX-E-ANCHOR-POSITION-INVALID.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 assigns NO row to this defect class. Anchors and References section 7.2 tabulates severities for three anchor conditions — a target that does not exist, a position exceeding the target's text length, and an id collision — and a structurally invalid position is none of them, so no disposition is inferred here. Tracked as a specification gap.
CDX-E-ANCHOR-POSITION-INVALID.note: Distinct from CDX-E-ANCHOR-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE, which Anchors and References section 7.2 DOES tabulate and which therefore carries a concrete disposition. The two also differ in when they can fire: this code is reported whether or not the target id resolves, because a malformed position is malformed either way and gating it on resolution would let a dangling reference conceal a second defect; the out-of-range code needs a resolved, text-bearing target to have a length to exceed. Section 7.3 states each of these as a MUST, so a null disposition records that the specification omits the disposition, never that a consumer may ignore the defect. ONE CODE ACROSS ALL THREE REFERENCE ROWS, deliberately, where the out-of-range arm carries three (this code, CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE, CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE). That arm is split because its rows assign different frozen/published dispositions, and an append-only vocabulary cannot separate them later; a null disposition contributes nothing to a verdict in any state and so cannot diverge between rows at all. Splitting this one would publish three codes recording the same absence of a rule. If an erratum closes the gap it may do so unevenly, per row — at which point the split becomes necessary and the successor codes are added then, this entry being deprecated rather than re-pointed.

CDX-E-ANCHOR-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE.summary: A CORE ANCHOR in hashed content addresses a position past the end of its target block's text content — a `link` mark `href` whose `offset`, or range `end`, is greater than the number of code points in the concatenated text of the text-bearing block it targets.
CDX-E-ANCHOR-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling core anchor reference in hashed content — a `link`/`anchor` Content Anchor (Anchors and References section 7.2) — WARNING in draft/review). That row cites section 7.2, whose table lists "Offset/range exceeds target block text length" among the conditions it governs, at Warning in draft/review and Error in frozen/published.
CDX-E-ANCHOR-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE.note: STATE-VARYING: WARNING in DRAFT/REVIEW, escalating to INTEGRITY-ERROR on FROZEN/PUBLISHED (Anchors and References section 7.2). The escalation is deferred to B3 via State Machine section 5.4.2 note 3; every B1b fixture is a draft. A position EQUAL to the text length is valid, not out of range: section 7.3 says a position MUST NOT EXCEED the length, and a half-open interval ending at the length selects through the final character. Length is counted in Unicode code points (section 3: "A character is one Unicode scalar value"), so a reader measuring UTF-16 code units mis-reports every block containing an astral character. SCOPED TO THE CORE-ANCHOR ROW, one of THREE out-of-range codes rather than one across every reference field. An out-of-range position takes the same section 5.4.2 row as a dangling target in the same field, because the row is a property of what the reference is FOR and not of which half of it failed — so the extension-block fields take CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE and the `academic:*-ref` marks take CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE, mirroring CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-DANGLING and CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-DANGLING. One code across all three rows would publish a single disposition for rows that diverge: this row escalates when frozen while the cross-reference row is WARNING in every state, so post-B3 an `academic:theorem-ref` whose target was MISSING would stay a WARNING while one naming a merely stale offset became an INTEGRITY-ERROR.

CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RA.summary: A Content Anchor URI carried in an extension BLOCK field — `academic:proof` `of`, an `academic:theorem` `uses[]` element, or a `semantic:ref` or `presentation:reference` `target` — addresses a position past the end of its target block's text content.
CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RA.clause: Anchors and References sections 3, 7.2, 7.3, 11; Academic Extension section 9; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RA.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling core anchor reference in hashed content — WARNING in draft/review), the same row CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-DANGLING takes for the same fields. That row cites Anchors and References section 7.2, whose table lists "Offset/range exceeds target block text length" among the conditions it governs.
CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RA.note: STATE-VARYING as CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-DANGLING, and CONTESTED for exactly the reason that entry records: whether these extension-block fields are core anchors (Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 5 rewrites them into the same relabelled namespace as a `link` mark, and section 5.4.2's extension-cross-reference carve-out names only MARKS) or cross-references (Anchors and References section 11 groups them with the cross-reference mechanisms). Draft and review are WARNING under either reading, so the two differ only in the frozen column. Its own code rather than sharing CDX-E-ANCHOR-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE, on the same reasoning that gave the dangling arm its own code: separating them lets B3 settle the frozen column without re-pointing a published code, which the compatibility policy forbids. WIDER THAN ITS DANGLING SIBLING'S CONTEST, and the asymmetry is deliberate. Academic Extension section 9 settles the frozen column for a DANGLING `academic:proof` `of` or `academic:theorem` `uses` target, so CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-DANGLING's contest covers only two of its four fields. Section 9 does NOT reach the position case: both of its dispositions are scoped to "a dangling target", and neither mentions an offset or a range. All four fields are therefore contested HERE. What section 9 does settle bears on this entry the other way: by classifying `of` and `uses` as "academic cross-references resolved at render time" it moves them INTO the section 7.2-versus-section 5.4.2 conflict that CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE records, rather than out of it. Both position entries therefore say the same thing about section 9's reach, which is the point — they are reading one sentence. The STRUCTURAL arm is not split — a structurally invalid position on any of these fields is CDX-E-ANCHOR-POSITION-INVALID, whose disposition is null in every row. See that entry for why.

CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RA.summary: An extension cross-reference mark resolved at render time — an `academic:theorem-ref`, `academic:equation-ref`, or `academic:algorithm-ref` — carries a `target` Content Anchor URI addressing a position past the end of its target block's text content.
CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RA.clause: Anchors and References sections 3, 7.2, 7.3; Academic Extension section 9; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RA.dispositionClause: WARNING in draft/review, which BOTH candidate readings assign; see the note for the frozen/published column, which they contest. Reading one: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling extension cross-reference resolved at render time — WARNING in every state), the row CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-DANGLING takes for these same marks, extended to the position half of the same field. Reading two: Anchors and References section 7.2, whose table lists "Offset/range exceeds target block text length" at Warning in draft/review and Error in frozen/published.
CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RA.note: CLASSIFICATION RECORDED AS CONTESTED, and unlike its two siblings the contest here is a SPECIFICATION CONFLICT rather than a reading of one clause (docs/design-decisions.md OQ-011). Anchors and References section 7.2's table is keyed on the CONDITION and not on the field carrying it, section 7.3 repeats the rule unqualified, and section 11 names these marks as consumers of the same anchor system — so section 7.2 tabulates this very defect and escalates it when frozen. Against that, State Machine section 5.4.2 gives these marks a row that is WARNING in EVERY state, and its integrity-binding preamble keys that on the KIND of reference rather than on the failure: such a mark is resolved at render time, so a defect in it degrades rendering only while the signed bytes remain intact and hash-verified. Note section 5.4.2's row covers the mark whose "target does not resolve" and so does not literally reach a position, while the core-anchor row reaches the position case through its own section 7.2 citation — which is exactly why the two rows can diverge here and cannot for CDX-E-ANCHOR-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE. Two further texts bear on it. Anchors and References section 7.2 CLOSES by mapping its own table onto the disposition vocabulary with no field qualifier — "These severities are the WARNING and INTEGRITY-ERROR dispositions of State Machine section 5.4" — the strongest support for the escalating reading. Against it, Academic Extension section 9 makes the opposite choice for the NEIGHBOURING failure in these same marks: although a `*-ref` `target` "uses Content Anchor syntax", the marks "are extension cross-references resolved at render time, so a dangling target is a rendering-degradation WARNING in all states (State Machine section 5.4), not the INTEGRITY-ERROR of a dangling core anchor". Section 9's very next sentence extends the same disposition to `academic:proof` `of` and `academic:theorem` `uses`, and THERE it rejects the alternative by section number — "not the FROZEN/PUBLISHED Error that Anchors and References section 7.2 assigns a dangling core anchor". That is kind-beating-condition, chosen explicitly and against section 7.2 by name; it does not literally reach the position case, so it does not settle this one, but it makes the readings unequal and gives any settling erratum a third site to amend. Both readings give WARNING in draft/review, so only the frozen column is contested, and this entry's scalar disposition is unaffected either way (see dispositionNote). Separating this arm from CDX-E-ANCHOR-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE is what leaves B3 free to settle that column without re-pointing a published code, which the compatibility policy forbids — the split had to happen before a disposition was published, not after.

CDX-E-ANNOTATION-ANCHOR-POSITION-INVALID.summary: An anchor originating in an out-of-hash annotation layer carries a defective position — either structurally invalid (a range whose start is not less than its end, `offset` alongside `start`/`end`, a half range, a negative or non-integer value, a position on an `anchor`-mark target, or a position on a target that is not a text-bearing block) or addressing a position past the end of the target block's text content.
CDX-E-ANNOTATION-ANCHOR-POSITION-INVALID.clause: Anchors and References sections 2.2, 3, 7.3; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-ANNOTATION-ANCHOR-POSITION-INVALID.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling anchor originating in an out-of-hash annotation layer — a collaboration comment/change anchor or a phantom cluster anchor pointing into content — WARNING in both columns).
CDX-E-ANNOTATION-ANCHOR-POSITION-INVALID.note: STATE-INVARIANT, for the same reason as CDX-E-ANNOTATION-ANCHOR-DANGLING: the layer's bytes are bound by neither the document hash nor the manifest projection, so its failure cannot signal tampering. ONE code covers both the structural and the out-of-bounds arms here, and every anchor-bearing field of every out-of-hash layer, where hashed content splits the same defects four ways (CDX-E-ANCHOR-POSITION-INVALID, and one out-of-range code per reference row: CDX-E-ANCHOR-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE, CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE, CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-POSITION-OUT-OF-RANGE). Every one of those splits exists to keep two dispositions that MAY DIVERGE once the frozen/published column is lit in B3 separable under an append-only vocabulary — the structural arm is not tabulated by Anchors and References section 7.2 while the out-of-bounds one is, and the three reference rows do not agree with each other on the frozen column. Out of hash there is nothing to keep separable: every arm and every field takes this single row, WARNING in every state, so splitting would record distinctions the specification does not make.

CDX-E-ANNOTATION-ANCHOR-DANGLING.summary: An anchor originating in an out-of-hash annotation layer points at content that does not exist: a collaboration comment or change anchor, a change `position` block id, a phantom cluster anchor, or a core annotation anchor naming no defined identifier.
CDX-E-ANNOTATION-ANCHOR-DANGLING.clause: Anchors and References section 7.2; Extensions overview (Integrity Status of Extension Data); State Machine sections 5.4.2, 5.4.3
CDX-E-ANNOTATION-ANCHOR-DANGLING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling anchor originating in an out-of-hash annotation layer — WARNING in every state).
CDX-E-ANNOTATION-ANCHOR-DANGLING.note: STATE-INVARIANT: the anchoring layer's bytes are bound by neither the document hash nor the manifest projection, so a dangling anchor cannot signal tampering with signed content, in any state. Resolved only at the anchor positions the extension schemas DECLARE — `annotations[].anchor`, a comment or change `anchor`, a change `position.before`/`.after` block id, and a cluster `anchor`. A generic sweep for any `blockId` or `#` string would be wrong, not merely noisy: a phantom carries a full core content tree whose internal marks address the phantom's own interior, and a collaboration change record carries verbatim before/after block snapshots that legitimately name removed content. State Machine section 5.4.3 forbids escalating a defect confined to an out-of-hash layer's internal graph at all — such a defect is a layer-validity disposition, not an entry in the integrity table.

CDX-E-ID-COLLISION.summary: An identifier is defined more than once in the document's shared identifier namespace — block ids, `anchor` mark ids, equation-line ids and subfigure ids, which together form one namespace requiring uniqueness.
CDX-E-ID-COLLISION.clause: Anchors and References sections 4, 7.2; Document Hashing section 4.3.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-ID-COLLISION.dispositionClause: Anchors and References section 7.2 (ID collides with another ID in the shared namespace — Error in ALL states), whose severities section 7.2 maps onto the WARNING and INTEGRITY-ERROR dispositions of State Machine section 5.4.
CDX-E-ID-COLLISION.note: STATE-INVARIANT, and the only INTEGRITY-ERROR this layer assigns before B2/B3: because the disposition does not vary by state, it needs no projection-covering signature to be sound, unlike every deferred frozen/published escalation. Anchors and References section 7.2 makes a collision an Error in all states — a duplicate makes a reference ambiguous, so which content an anchor addresses is undecidable. The canonicalizer already refuses such a document (Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 5 rejects a duplicate id while relabelling), which is why this is reported before the document-ID recompute rather than left to surface as an unexplained inability to compute the id. The namespace is the one Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 5 DEFINES, which is a SUPERSET of what that item relabels: a `semantic:term` or `semantic:footnote` block's id is left as authored and is nonetheless a member, so a duplicate of one is still a collision and a Content Anchor URI still resolves against it. Identifiers addressing SEPARATE namespaces are not members and do not collide — a bibliography entry's citation key, and a `footnote` MARK's `id`, and a `glossary` mark's `ref`. Each is a separate identifier from the block id it resolves to — separate in NAMESPACE, and the two arms differ: Semantic Extension section 4.5.2 requires a `footnote` mark's `id` to be equal in VALUE to its `semantic:footnote` block's `id` when both are present, whereas a `glossary` mark carries no `id` at all and its `ref` resolves against a `semantic:term` block's `id` (or an external glossary file's, section 8.3).

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-COMPRESSION-METHOD-FORBIDD.summary: An archive entry declares a compression method outside the set Container Format section 3.2 permits (Store 0, Deflate 8, Zstandard 93).
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-COMPRESSION-METHOD-FORBIDD.clause: Container Format sections 3.2, 6.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-COMPRESSION-METHOD-FORBIDD.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (an archive entry declaring a compression method outside the set Container Format section 3.2 permits — REJECT in every state).
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-COMPRESSION-METHOD-FORBIDD.note: STATE-INVARIANT. Section 3.2's table is the complete permitted set, so an entry outside it makes the CONTAINER non-conformant — the same class as the ZIP-encryption and multi-volume rows, which are likewise section 3.1 violations that cannot be coherently loaded. The entry's bytes cannot be obtained, so neither its CRC-32 (section 6.1) nor any hash computed over it can be verified. Section 3.2 also forbids the failure mode this code was added to close: a reader MUST NOT infer a method from the data, and in particular MUST NOT treat an unrecognized method as Deflate — which either fails confusingly or appears to succeed on bytes it did not decode. Distinct from CDX-E-ARCHIVE-ENTRY-INTEGRITY-INDETERMINATE, which covers a PERMITTED method the reader has not implemented and is not a defect at all.

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-ENTRY-INTEGRITY-INDETERMIN.summary: An archive entry uses a compression method the specification permits but this reader does not implement, so the entry's integrity could be neither verified nor failed.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-ENTRY-INTEGRITY-INDETERMIN.clause: Container Format section 3.2; State Machine section 5.4.2 note 6
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-ENTRY-INTEGRITY-INDETERMIN.dispositionClause: NOT a document defect, and deliberately not given a disposition. Container Format section 3.2 makes Deflate mandatory to implement and Zstandard only RECOMMENDED, so a reader lacking Zstandard is conformant and the document is unaffected — exactly the treatment State Machine section 5.4.2 gives an unverifiable timestamp ("the timestamp is reported unverified; the document is unaffected"). Raising the verdict would fail a conformant document over the READER's capability envelope.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-ENTRY-INTEGRITY-INDETERMIN.note: A null disposition here means "reported, not counted", never "ignorable": State Machine section 5.4.2 note 6 requires that such an entry MUST NOT be reported as verified and MUST NOT be silently treated as clean. The finding exists precisely so an unverified entry is visible — before it, a Zstandard entry read by a Deflate-only reader passed every check with its CRC-32 and every hash over its bytes silently unverified. The conformance suite models the capability with `compression:zstd`, so a fixture using method 93 is scoped out of a reader without it rather than failed. NOTE ON THE NULL: this vocabulary now uses `disposition: null` for two distinct situations, and this entry is the second kind. A documented SPECIFICATION GAP (CDX-E-MANIFEST-REFERENCE-HASH-CONFLICT, and the manifest-value codes beside it) means the specification assigns no disposition and one is deliberately not inferred. This entry is a DELIBERATE NON-DEFECT: the specification does address it (State Machine section 5.4.2 note 6) and the answer is that the document is not at fault, so no disposition is the correct outcome rather than a missing one. Both are reported and neither raises the verdict; only this kind is a statement about the READER rather than the document.

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-ENTRY-UNDECODABLE.summary: An archive entry's data could not be decoded under its declared compression method, which the reader does implement — the bytes are corrupt or truncated.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-ENTRY-UNDECODABLE.clause: Container Format sections 3.2, 6.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-ENTRY-UNDECODABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Archive unreadable — REJECT in every state), read for an entry whose contents cannot be obtained, and consistent with the CRC-32 row: section 6.1 requires verifying each entry's CRC-32 and rejecting on mismatch, and an entry whose bytes will not decode can never satisfy that check.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-ENTRY-UNDECODABLE.note: STATE-INVARIANT, and a container-layer physical-corruption check that applies regardless of the entry's logical layer — the same framing section 5.4.2 gives the CRC-32 row. Distinct from CDX-E-ARCHIVE-CRC-MISMATCH, which requires bytes that DID decode and whose checksum then differed; here no checksum could be computed at all, so reporting a mismatch would misdescribe what happened. Distinct from CDX-E-ARCHIVE-UNREADABLE, whose published summary is scoped to the ARCHIVE structure (a missing End Of Central Directory record, a malformed central directory) and cannot be widened under the append-only policy. Nothing else in the reader owns this case: the local-header/central-directory cross-check compares names and existence only, and the decompression bound reads DECLARED sizes, so before this code such an entry reported clean.

CDX-E-PART-MISSING-BOUND.summary: A part the manifest references AND binds by hash cannot be obtained — absent from the archive, or present but unloadable: a declared `presentation[]` layer, an asset category's index file, or an asset the index lists.
CDX-E-PART-MISSING-BOUND.clause: State Machine section 5.4.2; Asset Embedding sections 3.1, 11.1; Presentation Layers section 12
CDX-E-PART-MISSING-BOUND.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Missing or unparseable referenced part bound by the document hash or manifest projection — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-PART-MISSING-BOUND.note: STATE-VARYING: WARNING in draft/review, INTEGRITY-ERROR on a frozen or published document, where the manifest projection a signature covers binds the missing part's hash — the escalation is deferred to B3 with every other state-keyed ceiling (State Machine section 5.4.2 note 3). Distinguished from CDX-E-PART-MISSING-UNBOUND by whether a hash binds the reference at all: a path-only reference binds nothing, so its target's absence cannot signal tampering. An asset LISTED in the index but absent from the archive belongs here rather than under CDX-E-ASSET-REFERENCE-DANGLING, because the reference still RESOLVES — Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 2 binds the index's declared hash into the document ID, not the asset's bytes — so the document ID is unaffected and only the bytes are missing (Asset Embedding section 11.1 item 1).

CDX-E-ASSET-INDEX-UNUSABLE.summary: A declared asset category's index file is present but cannot be used to resolve the category's assets: it does not parse, it is not an object, it carries no `assets` array, an entry declares a malformed hash, two entries resolve to one archive path under conflicting hashes, or the category key is not a valid path segment.
CDX-E-ASSET-INDEX-UNUSABLE.clause: Asset Embedding section 3.1; Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 2; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-ASSET-INDEX-UNUSABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Missing or unparseable referenced part bound by the document hash or manifest projection — WARNING in draft/review), read as covering a hash-bound part that is present but unusable. Asset Embedding section 3.1 requires each declared category to HAVE an index file; a file that cannot yield the category's assets does not provide one, so the same row governs and the same disposition follows.
CDX-E-ASSET-INDEX-UNUSABLE.note: STATE-VARYING as CDX-E-PART-MISSING-BOUND; the frozen/published escalation is B3. THE CLASSIFICATION IS A READING, recorded here rather than assumed silently: the erratum widened that row to "missing or unparseable", which transcribes this code's does-not-parse arm, but section 5.4.2 still has no row for an index that PARSES and yields no usable assets. The alternative — `disposition: null`, this vocabulary's convention for a defect the specification assigns no row (see CDX-E-MANIFEST-REFERENCE-HASH-CONFLICT) — is not the conservative choice here but the wrong one: a null disposition does not raise the document verdict, so a document whose asset category cannot be resolved at all would load indistinguishably from a clean one, which section 5.4.2's integrity-binding axis contradicts for material the manifest projection binds. The row "Missing or unparseable referenced part bound by the document hash or manifest projection" is the closest analogue and Asset Embedding section 3.1 makes having a usable index a MUST, so that row is taken and a dedicated one is raised as a specification question. (That citation formerly named the row by number, which rotted as soon as a row was inserted above it; the append-only policy now requires quoting a row's text instead.) Every cause listed makes the category INDETERMINATE: the document-ID recompute is skipped for it and its asset references are neither confirmed nor reported dangling, exactly as an unloadable Dublin Core part suspends the id check rather than recomputing over an empty basis.

CDX-E-ASSET-INDEX-HASH-MISMATCH.summary: An asset category's index file does not match the hash the manifest declares for it in `manifest.assets.<category>.hash`.
CDX-E-ASSET-INDEX-HASH-MISMATCH.clause: Asset Embedding sections 3.1, 8.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-ASSET-INDEX-HASH-MISMATCH.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 assigns the same pair of dispositions to both rows this defect can be read under — "File `hash` or document-ID mismatch" and "Asset hash mismatch (Asset Embedding section 8)" are each WARNING in draft/review and INTEGRITY-ERROR in frozen/published — so the classification does not affect the disposition. Asset Embedding section 8.1 step 3 names `manifest.assets.<category>.hash` as the index file's declared hash.
CDX-E-ASSET-INDEX-HASH-MISMATCH.note: STATE-VARYING; the frozen/published escalation is B3. This is the anchor of the whole category: because the index enumerates every asset's and every variant's own hash, hash-pinning the one index file transitively attests the category (Asset Embedding section 3.1), and a manifest-covering signature binds that index hash (Security Extension section 9.7). A mismatch here does NOT suspend the per-asset checks — the index's bytes exist and parse, so the hashes it carries are still verifiable, and reporting both is more informative than reporting the outer failure alone.

CDX-E-ASSET-HASH-MISMATCH.summary: An asset's stored bytes, or an image variant's, do not match the `hash` the category index declares for them.
CDX-E-ASSET-HASH-MISMATCH.clause: Asset Embedding sections 4.3, 8.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-ASSET-HASH-MISMATCH.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Asset hash mismatch, Asset Embedding section 8 — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-ASSET-HASH-MISMATCH.note: STATE-VARYING: INTEGRITY-ERROR on a frozen or published document (Asset Embedding section 8.1 step 4), deferred to B3. Covers a top-level asset and an image VARIANT alike, because Asset Embedding section 4.3 makes the variant — not the parent — what a viewer actually sees: without its own binding a swapped variant would substitute displayed content while the parent hash, the document ID and every signature still verify.

CDX-E-ASSET-VARIANT-MISSING.summary: An image variant the category index lists is absent from the archive.
CDX-E-ASSET-VARIANT-MISSING.clause: Asset Embedding section 4.3; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-ASSET-VARIANT-MISSING.dispositionClause: Asset Embedding section 4.3 ("Missing variants SHOULD produce a warning but MUST NOT prevent the image from being displayed"), whose severity maps onto the WARNING disposition of State Machine section 5.4.
CDX-E-ASSET-VARIANT-MISSING.note: STATE-INVARIANT, and deliberately NOT the escalating CDX-E-PART-MISSING-BOUND row that a missing top-level asset earns. Asset Embedding section 4.3 requires the reader to fall back to the full-resolution image, so the document still renders exactly the content it asserts: the absence degrades resolution selection, it does not withhold bound material. A variant that IS present but mismatched is a different matter and is CDX-E-ASSET-HASH-MISMATCH.

CDX-E-ASSET-INDEX-PATH-DIVERGENT.summary: A declared `manifest.assets.<category>.index` path differs from the derived location `assets/<category>/index.json`.
CDX-E-ASSET-INDEX-PATH-DIVERGENT.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (A declared `manifest.assets.<category>.index` that does not equal the derived location `assets/<category>/index.json` — REJECT in BOTH columns).
CDX-E-ASSET-INDEX-PATH-DIVERGENT.note: GAP CLOSED BY ERRATUM. This entry previously carried `disposition: null`, because section 5.4.2 assigned no row and Asset Embedding section 3.1 resolved the conflict leniently — "if an explicit `index` value disagrees with it the derived path governs" — leaving the document loadable with no stated disposition. The erratum deleted that sentence and added a REJECT row, so the null is filled rather than reclassified.
