The reason it is a REJECT and not a warning is the seam this code was minted to report: the manifest projection binds the DECLARED path's hash (Security Extension section 9.7, via the asset-index references) while the document ID is computed from the DERIVED path's bytes (Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 2 builds every asset archive path from the category key), so a signature would attest one file while identity depends on another. Rejecting the divergence closes the split without changing any projected bytes: for every loadable document the two paths name the same file.

CDX-E-ASSET-REFERENCE-DANGLING.summary: A content asset reference — an `image`/`svg` `src`, a `signature` `image`, or a `link` mark `href` naming an `assets/`-rooted path — resolves to no registered asset.
CDX-E-ASSET-REFERENCE-DANGLING.clause: Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 2; Asset Embedding section 3.2; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-ASSET-REFERENCE-DANGLING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling asset reference — a canonicalization error once the ID is computed — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-ASSET-REFERENCE-DANGLING.note: STATE-VARYING: INTEGRITY-ERROR on a frozen or published document, deferred to B3. Unlike the render-time cross-reference marks, this one is an integrity failure of hashed content: Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 2 REPLACES the reference with the asset's hash, so an unresolvable one makes the document's identity uncomputable, which is why section 5.4.2 defines the row as a canonicalization error. A reference marked `external`, carrying a URL scheme, or beginning with `#` is not an asset path and never fires this (Asset Embedding sections 3.2, 9.2). A reference into a category whose index could not be loaded is INDETERMINATE, not dangling, and is not reported.

CDX-E-PRESENTATION-HASH-MISMATCH.summary: A declared `manifest.presentation[]` layer's stored bytes do not match the `hash` the manifest declares for it.
CDX-E-PRESENTATION-HASH-MISMATCH.clause: Document Hashing section 6.3; Presentation Layers section 12; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-PRESENTATION-HASH-MISMATCH.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (File `hash` or document-ID mismatch — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-PRESENTATION-HASH-MISMATCH.note: STATE-VARYING; the frozen/published INTEGRITY-ERROR is B3. Separate from CDX-E-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH, whose published summary is specifically `manifest.content.hash` over the content part's bytes — conformance/errors.json is append-only, so that entry's meaning cannot be widened after publication. A presentation layer's hash IS bound into the manifest projection (Security Extension section 9.7), so on a frozen or published document a mismatch is caught by the signature as well; the dangling-reference row for the same file is NOT integrity-binding (see CDX-E-PRESENTATION-REFERENCE-DANGLING), and the two must not be conflated.

CDX-E-PRESENTATION-REFERENCE-DANGLING.summary: A presentation rule targets a content block that does not exist — a `pageElement` `blockId`, a `section` `blockRefs` entry, or a `flow` element's `blockIds` entry.
CDX-E-PRESENTATION-REFERENCE-DANGLING.clause: Presentation Layers sections 6.4, 13.4; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-PRESENTATION-REFERENCE-DANGLING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling presentation reference — a `blockId`, `blockRefs`, or `blockIds` targeting a non-existent content block — WARNING in BOTH columns).
CDX-E-PRESENTATION-REFERENCE-DANGLING.note: STATE-INVARIANT. Presentation Layers section 13.4 gives the reason: presentation sits outside the document-hash boundary (Document Hashing section 4.1a), so a dangling presentation reference degrades rendering but never impugns document integrity, in any state — the reader omits that rule and renders the affected content with default styling. The presentation FILE's own integrity is a separate matter, dispositioned by CDX-E-PRESENTATION-HASH-MISMATCH and CDX-E-PART-MISSING-BOUND. ENUMERATION GAP CLOSED BY ERRATUM: the section 5.4.2 row and Presentation Layers section 13.4 formerly named `blockId` and `blockRefs` only, though a flow element's `blockIds` references content blocks identically (section 6.4). Both now name all three, and section 13.4 states that they are the complete set of presentation fields that reference content blocks. No disposition changed — this code already covered all three.

CDX-E-PRESENTATION-UNDECLARED.summary: A presentation or precise-layout file is present in the archive but is not declared in `manifest.presentation[]`, so no hash binds it.
CDX-E-PRESENTATION-UNDECLARED.clause: Presentation Layers sections 12, 12.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-PRESENTATION-UNDECLARED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (A presentation or precise-layout file present in the archive but not declared in `manifest.presentation[]`, so no hash binds it and no manifest-covering signature attests it — WARNING in draft/review, INTEGRITY-ERROR on frozen/published).
CDX-E-PRESENTATION-UNDECLARED.note: ROW ADDED BY ERRATUM; STATE-VARYING. This entry previously reasoned its WARNING from section 5.4.2's preamble and Presentation Layers section 12 because the table carried no dedicated row, and recorded the reading rather than assuming it. The erratum added the row, at exactly the disposition that was inferred, so the draft/review WARNING is now transcribed rather than derived and the frozen/published INTEGRITY-ERROR is stated in the table — deferred to B3 with every other state-keyed ceiling. The frozen column matches what the rest of the specification already required: Presentation Layers sections 3.4 and 12 both scope the MUST-NOT-RENDER obligation to a frozen or published document, where a manifest-covering signature is mandatory and an undeclared layout is precisely what such a signature cannot attest. The finding reports the file's presence, never a judgement about rendering: the normative requirement is that a renderer MUST NOT treat it as authoritative appearance.

CDX-E-CONFIG-PART-MISSING.summary: A `{path, hash}` side file declared in an extension config slot — a semantic bibliography or glossary, an academic numbering configuration — cannot be obtained: absent from the archive, or present but unloadable.
CDX-E-CONFIG-PART-MISSING.clause: State Machine section 5.4.2; Security Extension section 9.7
CDX-E-CONFIG-PART-MISSING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Missing or unparseable referenced part bound by the document hash or manifest projection — WARNING in draft/review), which the erratum below settled as the governing row.
CDX-E-CONFIG-PART-MISSING.note: CLASSIFICATION SETTLED BY ERRATUM; STILL STATE-VARYING. The out-of-hash row formerly gave "a PATH-ONLY semantic/academic side file (bibliography, glossary, numbering)" as an example, contradicting its own qualifier: semantic.schema.json and academic.schema.json declare these references as a `fileReference` with `required: [path, hash]` and `additionalProperties: false`, and collectConfigFileReferences binds every such `{path, hash}` into the manifest projection (Security Extension section 9.7 — whose own schema says the binding exists to attest "academic numbering, semantic bibliography/glossary"), so a conformant declaration is never path-only. The erratum removed those examples from the out-of-hash row and stated that the hash-bound row governs. The draft/review disposition is unchanged at WARNING — both readings always agreed there — and the frozen/published column is therefore INTEGRITY-ERROR, deferred to B3 with every other state-keyed ceiling. This remains a separate code from CDX-E-PART-MISSING-BOUND, whose published summary enumerates a `presentation[]` layer, an asset index and an indexed asset rather than a config-slot side file.

CDX-E-CONFIG-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH.summary: A `{path, hash}` side file declared in an extension config slot does not match the hash declared for it.
CDX-E-CONFIG-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH.clause: Document Hashing section 6.3; Security Extension section 9.7; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-CONFIG-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (File `hash` or document-ID mismatch — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-CONFIG-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH.note: STATE-VARYING; the frozen/published escalation is B3. Separate from CDX-E-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH for the same append-only reason as CDX-E-PRESENTATION-HASH-MISMATCH: that code's published summary names `manifest.content.hash` specifically. Unlike CDX-E-CONFIG-PART-MISSING, this code's ROW is not contested — the file declares a hash, so comparing it against the stored bytes is the file-hash row on either reading of where the missing-file case belongs.

CDX-E-CITATION-REFERENCE-DANGLING.summary: A `citation` mark's `refs` entry names no entry in the document's AUTHORITATIVE bibliography source — the external `semantic/bibliography.json` when the manifest declares `semantic.bibliography`, otherwise the inline `entries` of a `semantic:bibliography` block.
CDX-E-CITATION-REFERENCE-DANGLING.clause: Semantic Extension section 4.4; Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 5; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-CITATION-REFERENCE-DANGLING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling extension cross-reference resolved at render time — a citation, glossary, footnote, or academic/legal cross-reference mark whose target does not resolve — WARNING in every state), which Semantic Extension section 4.4 restates for this mark: a `ref` that resolves against neither source "is a rendering-degradation WARNING in all states … never an integrity failure".
CDX-E-CITATION-REFERENCE-DANGLING.note: STATE-INVARIANT, for the reason section 5.4.2's preamble gives: the mark is resolved at render time to inject a label or number, so a dangling one degrades rendering only while the signed bytes remain intact and hash-verified. A separate code from CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-DANGLING, whose published summary enumerates the three `academic:*-ref` marks specifically and cannot be widened under the append-only policy. PRECEDENCE, NOT UNION: Semantic Extension section 4.4 makes the external file the SINGLE authoritative source when declared — "inline `entries` are not consulted, so the two cannot diverge" — so a `ref` naming an inline entry the declared file omits IS dangling. Unioning the two sources would report such a document clean. The namespace is not the content-anchor namespace either: Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 5 leaves a `semantic:bibliography` entry's CSL citation key as authored precisely because it addresses a separate one. When a declared side file could not be loaded the namespace is indeterminate, and no citation is reported dangling.

CDX-E-GLOSSARY-REFERENCE-DANGLING.summary: A `glossary` mark's `ref`, or a `semantic:term` block's `see` entry, names no term in the document's AUTHORITATIVE glossary source — `semantic/glossary.json` when the manifest declares `semantic.glossary`, otherwise the in-document `semantic:term` blocks.
CDX-E-GLOSSARY-REFERENCE-DANGLING.clause: Semantic Extension section 8.3; Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 5; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-GLOSSARY-REFERENCE-DANGLING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling extension cross-reference resolved at render time — WARNING in every state), which Semantic Extension section 8.3 restates for this mark: a `ref` or `see` resolving against neither source "is a rendering-degradation WARNING in all states … never an integrity failure".
CDX-E-GLOSSARY-REFERENCE-DANGLING.note: STATE-INVARIANT, as CDX-E-CITATION-REFERENCE-DANGLING, and a separate code from it so the two namespaces stay independently reportable. PRECEDENCE, NOT UNION, and the fallback is IN-DOCUMENT: Semantic Extension section 8.3 gives two rules — (1) a declared external glossary "is authoritative: … a `glossary` `ref` (or a `see`) resolves against the file's term `id`s"; (2) "Otherwise, the in-document `semantic:term` blocks are the source … a `glossary` `ref` (or a `see`) resolves against their `id`s." Modelling rule 2's namespace as empty would report a dangling reference on every document that defines its terms inline. TENSION RESOLVED BY ERRATUM: Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 5 formerly relabelled a `semantic:term` block's `id` to `b<n>` while leaving a `glossary` `ref` as authored, so the two could never match after canonicalization and section 8.3 rule 2 had effect only when read over RAW stored content. Item 5 now leaves such a block id as authored, so both sides match on the canonical form as well. Resolution still runs over raw stored content — that is the resolver's input — but it now AGREES with the canonical form instead of diverging from it, and section 8.3 rule 2 needed no rewording. When a declared side file could not be loaded the namespace is indeterminate and nothing is reported dangling.

CDX-E-FOOTNOTE-REFERENCE-DANGLING.summary: A `footnote` mark resolves to no `semantic:footnote` block — neither by `id` nor by its `number` or `symbol` marker.
CDX-E-FOOTNOTE-REFERENCE-DANGLING.clause: Semantic Extension section 4.5.2; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-FOOTNOTE-REFERENCE-DANGLING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling extension cross-reference resolved at render time — a citation, glossary, footnote, or academic/legal cross-reference mark whose target does not resolve — WARNING in every state), which Semantic Extension section 4.5.2 restates for this mark: "a footnote mark that resolves to no block is likewise a WARNING, never an integrity failure".
CDX-E-FOOTNOTE-REFERENCE-DANGLING.note: STATE-INVARIANT, as the sibling extension cross-reference codes. THE NAMESPACE IS PURELY IN-DOCUMENT and therefore never indeterminate: section 4.5.2 gives footnotes no side file, unlike the citation and glossary arms, where a declared-but-unloadable file suppresses reporting. RESOLUTION ORDER (section 4.5.2): id match takes precedence when both the mark and a block carry an `id`; otherwise the marker matches — a `number` mark to the block with the equal `number`, a `symbol` mark to the block with the equal `symbol`. That rule became satisfiable on the CANONICAL form only once Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 5 stopped relabelling a `semantic:footnote` block id (DD-022): before that the mark kept `fn1` while the block became `b0`, so the rule had effect only over raw stored bytes. A READING IS RECORDED, NOT SETTLED: where a mark carries an `id` matching no block, this implementation falls back to the marker rather than reporting immediately. Section 4.5.2's "resolves to its `semantic:footnote` block by a single key" also supports the strict reading, under which the unmatched `id` is itself the dangling reference. The divergence is warn-versus-SILENT, not one WARNING against another: under the charitable reading nothing is reported at all. Nor do the two disagree only where a MUST is breached — a mark carrying an unmatched `id` against a single block that carries NONE breaches nothing (section 4.5.2's id MUST is conditioned on "when both the mark and a block carry an `id`"), and the readings still diverge there. What makes the choice safe to record rather than settle is that no published fixture or vector carries the disputed shape, and the fixture comparator is a subset check, so a reader implementing the strict reading still passes the corpus. Tracked as OQ-009.

CDX-E-FOOTNOTE-REFERENCE-AMBIGUOUS.summary: A `footnote` mark's `number` or `symbol` marker matches more than one `semantic:footnote` block, so the marker does not identify a single target.
CDX-E-FOOTNOTE-REFERENCE-AMBIGUOUS.dispositionClause: Semantic Extension section 4.5.2 states the disposition directly, in the State Machine section 5.4 vocabulary: "A reader that finds a marker resolving to more than one block treats it as a rendering-degradation WARNING (section 11) and resolves to the first block in document order".
CDX-E-FOOTNOTE-REFERENCE-AMBIGUOUS.note: NOT A DANGLING REFERENCE, and a separate code for that reason: the mark DOES resolve — to the first block in document order — so the defect is that the reference is not deterministic, not that its target is absent. WHICH obligation was breached depends on the document, and it is not always the uniqueness MUST: section 4.5.2 qualifies that MUST with "absent `id`s", so two blocks sharing a marker while carrying DISTINCT `id`s breach nothing — that is exactly the arrangement the section blesses when it says a bare marker "can legitimately repeat". What the MARK then breaches is the other half of the same sentence: an author who repeats a marker MUST "give each footnote a unique `id` and reference it by `id`". The reader rule this code implements is stated independently of both, and fires whenever a marker resolves to more than one block. State Machine section 5.4.2 assigns no row of its own to this class; the disposition is transcribed from section 4.5.2, which states it in section 5.4's own vocabulary, exactly as section 8.3 restates the glossary arm's. THE FIRST-IN-DOCUMENT-ORDER HALF IS NOT MODELLED AT ALL, and deliberately: selecting a target is a RENDERER behaviour, and this layer performs no selection — it reports the ambiguity and stops. What IS pinned, in scripts/test-document-verdict.ts, is the set of must-NOT-report properties the fixture comparator cannot express, being a subset check over reported findings: that an `id` match suppresses an otherwise-ambiguous marker, that an ambiguous marker is not also reported dangling, and that duplicate markers no mark references report nothing. SCOPE: reported when a MARK's marker is ambiguous, which is the case section 4.5.2's reader rule addresses. Two blocks sharing a marker that no mark references violate the same MUST but have no stated reader disposition, and are not reported here.
